title: Prioritization canvas for enterprise SDK onboarding and streaming/auth ergonomics
creator: Marisol Ruiz
description:
Problem: Enterprise prospects and early customers continue to file varied SDK requests: language bindings gaps, non-idiomatic streaming APIs, and inconsistent auth/credential-rotation patterns. Without a clear prioritization approach we risk either over-indexing small surface ergonomics or delaying high-impact infra changes (e.g., credential refresh + resumable streams) that unlock enterprise adoption.

Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable prioritization canvas to triage SDK/client requests (non-bug) focused on language support, streaming ergonomics, and auth/credential patterns. Deliverables: 1) a scoring rubric and decision matrix; 2) mapped backlog of customer asks with recommended outcomes (Build / Design doc / Defer / Docs-only); 3) recommended quick wins for Q2 that reduce onboarding lift for 3 strategic enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas defined and documented in Confluence with scoring fields: adoption_leverage, engineering_cost, security_compliance_risk, customer_sla_urgency, telemetry_needs, fallback_complexity
Top 12 outstanding SDK requests (from support, solutions, AE intake) are scored and a recommended disposition assigned
Stakeholders (Solutions, Eng SDK leads, Security) reviewed rubric and provided sign-off or recorded objections
A 6-week plan with owners and acceptance criteria for 2 P1 items and 3 P2 quick wins is published
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Decided canvas should weight customer_revenue_exposure and security_compliance equally for enterprise-tier asks
2026-03-03: Agreed to treat language bindings that unlock Dedicated/Private deployments as higher priority
2026-03-08: Chose Build for credential-refresh + streaming-resume; Docs-only for one-off small language adaptor requests
comments: 2026-02-21 (Marisol): Collected initial 18 intake items from PM inbox, Solutions, and Support. Common themes: (1) token rotation + long-lived streams, (2) idiomatic streaming SDK for Java/.NET, (3) telemetry hooks for per-session cost attribution.
2026-02-26 (Liam): Draft rubric attached to Confluence. Need ENG SDK leads to estimate effort ranges. Pinging Chen Wei and Asha Patel for cost estimates.

2026-03-01 (Chen Wei): Quick scan: credential-rotation work is ~3 sprint weeks; Java streaming refactor is ~8 sprint weeks with potential infra changes for resumable state; Go binding for session-resume is ~2 sprint weeks.

2026-03-05 (Asha): Security flagged credential refresh flow needs KMS integration review for Private customers. Recommend security_review_required=true for any Build disposition that touches token lifecycle.
2026-03-09 (Marisol): Updated canvas weights based on feedback. Scheduling stakeholder sync 2026-03-12 to finalize top 3 priorities.

2026-03-10 (Liam): Added recommended Q2 quick wins: (a) Reference implementation for bearer-token rotation in Python SDK (docs + snippet), (b) telemetry labels in client for per-session cost tagging, (c) Java streaming ergonomics RFC kickoff
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Building a full idiomatic streaming SDK for multiple languages increases long-term maintenance burden; tradeoff: prioritize a canonical reference for Java and Python first.
- Enabling resumable streams + token refresh improves reliability for enterprise but requires infra changes to how KV-cache and session state are recorded; extra ops/observability work needed.
- Documentation-only dispositions reduce engineering workload but increase short-term support overhead and may slow sales cycles for customers who want end-to-end samples.
next_steps: Finalize scoring for top 12 intake items by 2026-03-18
Create two RFCs: (1) Credential rotation + token refresh pattern (owner: Chen Wei), (2) Streaming resume API shape for Java and Python (owner: Asha Patel)
Schedule 1:1 with Solutions lead for the three strategic customers to validate recommended dispositions by 2026-03-22
Spin up 'Docs & Snippets' task for Python bearer-token rotation (owner: Liam) to deliver by 2026-04-01
notes_for_engineering: When estimating, provide range (S/M/L) and call out infra changes required (runtime, routing, cache invalidation). Flag any unbounded risk such as cross-region session-state replication. Include perf regression acceptance criteria for streaming ergonomics work.
customer_examples: Acme Analytics (enterprise, Dedicated) - blocks on token rotation for long-running ingestion jobs
Nexa Legal (regulated, Private) - requires SSO + explicit audit trails for SDK auth flows
Crest Health (pilot) - requests Java streaming client with reconnect semantics and lower-latency callbacks
